The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the equivariant
constructible and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Let $G=\prod_v\mathrm{GL}_{n_v}(\mathbb C)$,
let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, and use bounded algebraically constructible complexes of
$k$-sheaves in the analytic topology, in the equivariant derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(-;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].
All functors are derived.

**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, use the general linear Stiefel approximations $U$ and their geometric quotients
supplied by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
with $b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$. In each fixed degree, once the supplied
bounded-Hom comparison applies, the group is the stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$. Comparison on products of sufficiently acyclic
resolutions makes it independent of the chosen such stage. Other free smooth models require
the same bounded-Hom and quotient hypotheses; freeness alone does not assert stabilization. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Correspondences.** Let $f_i:X_i\to E$ be finitely many proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps
with $X_i$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d_i$. Put $Z_{ij}=X_i\times_EX_j$ (reduced
analytically), $T_{ijk}=X_i\times_EX_j\times_EX_k$, and let $h:T_{ijk}\to Z_{ik}$ forget the
middle point; it is proper, being the base change of $f_j$
([[lem-proper-stable-base-change]]). The first coordinate is the source.
For $a\in H_p^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij})$, $b\in H_q^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{jk})$, define
$$a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^{!}(a\boxtimes b)\in H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik}).$$
Here $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ is the refined oriented middle-diagonal operation on supports of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]]: it
restricts the external class to $T_{ijk}$ by the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TX_j$
of $X_j\hookrightarrow X_j\times X_j$. It is defined on arbitrary closed supports; no
transversality of $Z_{ij}$ and $Z_{jk}$ is assumed. Proper pushforward is the dualizing trace.
The ordered coordinates are $(i,j,j,k)$, and the two middle factors are contracted without a
permutation. If intermediate indices differ, the product is set to zero. Put degree $d_i+d_j-p$
on the $(i,j)$ corner. The normalized diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ has corner degree zero.

**Sheaf model.** The sheaf model of the refined Thom operation uses the exchange morphism
$v'^*u^!\to u'^!v^*$ for the middle Cartesian square: with $u:Z_{ij}\to X_j$,
$v:Z_{jk}\to X_j$, $T=Z_{ij}\times_{X_j}Z_{jk}$ and projections $v':T\to Z_{ij}$,
$u':T\to Z_{jk}$, the morphism is obtained as the adjunction mate of proper base change
$v^*u_!\xrightarrow{\sim}u'_!v'^*$. Explicitly, its value at $C$ is adjoint to
$u'_!v'^*u^!C\to v^*u_!u^!C\to v^*C$, the first map being inverse base change and the
second the exceptional counit. It is a morphism, not an asserted isomorphism for arbitrary supports.
Its orientation is fixed by the Thom class restricting to $+1$ on every positively
complex-oriented normal fiber. Agreement of this model with the stated refined geometric
operation, and compatibility with composition, are proved in
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] after the
foundational six-functor inputs are available.

**Well-formedness.** The definition is independent of the chosen sufficiently acyclic Stiefel stage
because the stable Borel value exists and the product-resolution comparisons are coherent by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the product is
defined because the refined middle-diagonal operation of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] is
defined on arbitrary closed supports and $h$ is proper, so its dualizing trace is available; the
degree bookkeeping is fixed by the pure complex dimension $d_j$ of the middle factor. The claim
that the sheaf model and the geometric operation agree, and that the product is compatible with
composition and units, is not assumed here: it is the content of
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]], which is
recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that theorem depends on this
definition. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the cited suppliers, including proper
base-change stability; their descent, injective, Thom and Borel constructions declare it;
the definition itself introduces no further choice principle.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has
characteristic zero, and that a finite product
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups
acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]).
For equivariant algebraic maps between such varieties, the coherent ordinary
six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category
$D^b_{G,c}$:

1. the functors $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!$ are defined on $D^b_{G,c}$, with
   $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, and the tensor and internal-Hom
   adjunction $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$;
2. composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection
   formula and the trace hold, and for a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$,
   $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ the exchange
   $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey
   Cartesian pasting; proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$;
3. the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary
   $\omega_X$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]],
   and for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ one has
   $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$; this is not the unnormalized quotient-stack
   dualizing shift.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, and use $E_T=(E_{S^1})^r$, the product of the right Milnor join models, with $BT=E_T/T$. For the $i$th coordinate character $\chi_i([t_1,\ldots,t_r])=\exp(2\pi i t_i)$, let $L_i=E_T\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_i}$ be the associated complex line bundle over $BT$, with the right diagonal equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi_i(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_i=c_1(L_i)\in H^2(BT;\mathbb Q)$. Then
$$
BT\cong(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r,\qquad H^*(BT;\mathbb Q)\cong\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r],\qquad |u_i|=2.
$$
Every smooth character $\chi:T\to S^1$ is uniquely $\chi_{\mathbf n}([t])=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i n_it_i)$ for $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb Z^r$, and its associated line satisfies $c_1(L_{\chi_{\mathbf n}})=\sum_i n_i u_i$. In particular a nontrivial character has a nonzero degree-two class. For each $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, $H_q(BT;k)$ is finite-dimensional in every degree $q$. For $r=0$, $BT$ is a point and its rational cohomology is $\mathbb Q$.

derivations.claim: Since $T=(\mathrm{GL}_1)^r$, [F1] supplies the normalized equivariant Borel–Moore groups and the stable scalar-frame construction. For $U_m=(\mathbb C^{m+1}\setminus\{0\})^r$, the quotient is $B_m=(\mathbb{CP}^m)^r$ and $\dim_{\mathbb C}U_m-\dim_{\mathbb C}T=rm$, giving the stated degree shift. AC is inherited from [F1] and is the only choice assumption added here.

The polar decomposition $T\cong K\times(\mathbb R_{>0})^r$ makes $K\hookrightarrow T$ a homotopy equivalence. Choose one contractible free $T$-space $E$; it is also free for $K$, and $E/K\to E/T$ has contractible fiber $T/K$. The Borel fibrations $(E\times X)/K\to E/K$ and $(E\times X)/T\to E/T$ have common fiber $X$, with identity map on that fiber. Their homotopy exact sequences therefore make $(E\times X)/K\to(E\times X)/T$ a weak equivalence. Model independence of the universal free contractible space identifies this with the product right Milnor model and the algebraic-torus approximation in [F1].

By [F3], each nontrivial character has $u_\chi=\sum_i n_i u_i\neq0$ in the polynomial domain $R_T$. Therefore finite products of such classes remain nonzero, and concatenating two finite products shows that $S_T$ contains $1$, is multiplicatively closed, and excludes $0$. The localization by fractions is consequently defined.

The operations in the Definition are the proper pushforward, open restriction, and support maps of [F2]; the cap action is the action of Borel cohomology through $E_K\times_KX\to B_K$. For smooth pure complex dimension $d$, the normalized dualizing object restricts to $\mathbb Q_X[2d]$, so the complex orientation gives $[X]_T$ degree $2d$. These constructions respect the stable comparison of [F1].

The inclusion $K\subset T$ gives the same topological Borel construction up to homotopy. For each algebraic character $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$, let $L_\chi=E_K\times_K\mathbb C_{\chi|_K}\to B_K$, with right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_\chi=c_1(L_\chi)$. For the coordinate characters $\chi_i$ and $u_i=u_{\chi_i}$, the coefficient ring is $R_T=H^*(B_K;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, with $|u_i|=2$ and $u_\chi=\sum_i n_i u_i$ for $\chi(t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$. Let $S_T$ be the multiplicative set consisting of $1$ and finite products of $u_\chi$ for nontrivial $\chi$.

Let $H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{T,c}(X;\mathbb Q)}(\mathbb Q_X,\omega_X^T[-j])$, where $\omega_X^T$ is the normalized equivariant dualizing object whose restriction is the ordinary dualizing object $\omega_X$, without a quotient-stack dimension shift. Equivalently, this is the stable value in degree $j$ of $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{j+2rm}(X_m;\mathbb Q)$, where $U_m=(\mathbb C^{m+1}\setminus\{0\})^r$ has the free right scalar $T$-action, $X_m=(U_m\times X)/T$ uses $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$, and the supplied bounded-Hom comparison is taken in its stable range. The ring $R_T$ acts by pullback from $B_K$ and cap product. For an $R_T$-module $M$, $S_T^{-1}M$ consists of fractions $m/s$ with $m\in M$, $s\in S_T$, and $m/s=m'/s'$ exactly when some $t\in S_T$ satisfies $t(s'm-sm')=0$; addition and scalar multiplication are the induced fraction operations. Proper equivariant maps induce degree-preserving pushforwards, invariant open inclusions induce Borel–Moore restrictions, and a smooth pure $d$-dimensional complex variety has its complex-oriented fundamental class $[X]_T$ in degree $2d$. For $r=0$, $R_T=\mathbb Q$ and $S_T=\{1\}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly as in the general Thom theorem, and let
$\xi\to B$ be an $R$-oriented numerable real rank-$n$ vector bundle over a
base in the scope of that theorem. Let $u_\xi\in H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$ be its
normalized Thom class, let
$$j^*:H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)\longrightarrow H^n(D(\xi);R)$$ be the relative-to-absolute map of the pair sequence, and let $s:B\to D(\xi)$ be the zero section. The **Euler class** of $\xi$ is $$e(\xi)=e_{\rm Th}(\xi):=s^*j^*(u_\xi)\in H^n(B;R).$$
This is the class already introduced in
[[def-thom-euler-class-of-an-oriented-vector-bundle]]: on this page we write
$e(\xi)$ for it, and the shorthand $s^*u_\xi$ always means the composite
$s^*j^*(u_\xi)$, the relative-to-absolute map being understood. For rank zero
with supplied orientation $o\in H^0(B;R)$, normalization gives $u_\xi=o$ and
$j$ and $s$ are identities, so
$$e(0_B,o)=o\in H^0(B;R).$$
In particular, the standard unit orientation gives $e(0_B,1)=1$.
For $R=\mathbb F_2$ every real bundle is canonically $\mathbb F_2$-oriented by
[[def-r-oriented-vector-bundle-and-orientation-local-system]], so in that
case $e_2(\xi):=e(\xi)\in H^n(B;\mathbb F_2)$ is defined for every real
bundle in the Thom scope; for $R=\mathbb Z$ the class depends on the chosen
integral orientation, and reversing the orientation negates it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the analytic six-functor and equivariant constructible suppliers below. In the analytic constructible six-functor setting, let $M$ be the analytic space of a smooth complex algebraic variety of pure dimension $d$, and let $q:A\to M$, $u:B\to M$ be morphisms of complex algebraic varieties with fiber product $T=A\times_MB$; write $a:T\to A$ and $b:T\to B$ for the projections, so that $qa=ub$ and the square is Cartesian. Assume the supplied duality construction has localization, tensor–Hom adjunction, coherent exchange maps, and the smooth orientation normalized by the positive compactly supported generator on a complex coordinate ball ([[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]], [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]]), with its equivariant constructible form supplied by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]. The refined pullback of dualizing classes on the support $A\times B$ by the ambient middle diagonal $M\to M\times M$ is the operation induced by the mate $\mathrm{ex}:a^*q^!\to b^!u^*$ of the base-change morphism $u^*q_!\to b_!a^*$ of this square, after tensor evaluation and dualizing transitivity. derivations.claim: The set $D(f)$ is $T$-invariant because $f(t\cdot x)=\chi(t)f(x)$. On its Borel construction, define $s([e,x])=[e,f(x)]$ in the associated character line. This is well-defined: replacing $(e,x)$ by $(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$ replaces $f(x)$ by $f(t^{-1}\cdot x)=\chi(t)^{-1}f(x)$, exactly the right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$. Since $f$ never vanishes on $D(f)$, $s$ is a nowhere-zero section and trivializes that line bundle. The same formula trivializes its restriction to every $T$-invariant open $V\subseteq D(f)$.

On each finite Borel approximation, the first Chern class of the trivialized line is zero. By [F2] this is the Euler class of the line, and by [F3] its cap action on the approximating Borel–Moore groups is zero. The stable comparison in [F1] therefore gives $u_\chi\cap\beta=0$ for every $\beta\in H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(D(f);\mathbb Q)$, and the identical argument holds on $V$.

Since $\chi$ is nontrivial, $u_\chi\in S_T$ is invertible after localization. For any class $\beta$, its localized image satisfies $\beta/1=(u_\chi\cap\beta)/u_\chi=0$ by step 2.1. The localized groups on both $D(f)$ and $V$ consequently vanish. If the opposite character convention is used, the class is $-u_\chi$, which is also in $S_T$ up to the unit $-1$ and has the same annihilation consequence.

derivations.claim: Fix a member $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the invariant affine cover. Choose finitely many algebra generators of $A$. The algebraic $T$-action makes $A$ a rational $T$-comodule, so the coaction of each generator is a finite Laurent sum and the generator is a finite sum of character eigenfunctions. Replacing the generators by these finitely many eigencomponents still generates $A$, since their sums recover the original generators. The fixed ideal in $A$ is generated by its nontrivial-weight subspace: the coaction sends a weight-$\chi$ element $f$ to $f\otimes\chi$, so the equalizer with the trivial coaction kills $f$ when $\chi\ne1$, and the quotient by all such elements has only weight-zero functions and hence trivial action. The ideal generated by the nontrivial-weight algebra generators contains every nonzero-weight polynomial in the generators, since each monomial of nonzero total weight has a nonzero-weight factor. Thus $U\setminus F$ is covered by the finitely many invariant principal opens $D(f)$ for those generators.

Taking these principal opens over the finitely many affine charts gives a finite invariant open cover $\{D_a\}$ of $X\setminus F$. Every nonempty finite intersection is a $T$-invariant open subset of at least one $D_a$; [F2] therefore makes its localized Borel–Moore groups zero in every degree.

For a finite invariant open cover of $X\setminus F$, the augmented Čech complex with terms $j_{I!}\mathbb Q_{D_I}$, where $D_I$ is an intersection and $j_I:D_I\hookrightarrow X\setminus F$ is open, resolves the constant equivariant sheaf. At a point the indices containing it form a nonempty simplex, whose augmented cochain complex is contracted by its least index. Applying derived Hom into the normalized dualizing object gives a finite Čech spectral sequence for Borel–Moore homology: open base change identifies each term with the Borel–Moore group of an intersection $D_I$. Those groups vanish after localization by [F2]. Since the Čech filtration is finite and localization is exact by [F4], the abutment $S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X\setminus F;\mathbb Q)$ is zero for every $j$.

The closed/open localization sequence for $i:F\hookrightarrow X$ and $X\setminus F$ contains $S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_{j+1}(X\setminus F)\to S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(F)\xrightarrow{i_*}S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X)\to S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X\setminus F)$. derivations.claim: By [F1], $F$ is smooth and $T_xF=(T_xX)^T$. The quotient $T_xX/T_xF$ therefore has no invariant vector. On an affine open of a connected fixed component the base ring has trivial $T$-action, so the coaction on the finite-rank normal bundle is linear over that ring. Each of finitely many local module generators has finite character support; the character-coefficient projections are orthogonal idempotents summing to the identity. Their images are locally free direct summands. These decompositions agree on overlaps because the projections are defined by the group coaction. The zero-weight image has zero fiber at every point by $T_xF=(T_xX)^T$, so $\nu_F$ is the finite direct sum of nontrivial character subbundles. Thus $i$ is a closed regular embedding with the stated complex normal bundle.

The complex normal orientation gives the refined Gysin map in the normalized Borel–Moore grading. The Thom class is normalized to restrict to the positive complex-oriented generator on every normal fiber, so $i^![X]_T=[F]_T$. A $K$-invariant tubular neighborhood of each fixed component identifies the embedding locally in the Borel construction with the zero section of its normal bundle. By [F3] and the Thom class in [F4], this zero-section operation satisfies $i^!i_*\beta=e_T(\nu_F)\cap\beta$; the degree is lowered by twice the complex codimension $c$. The result is independent of the chosen tubular neighborhood because the refined exchange and orientation comparisons are canonical.

Now let $F_0$ be a connected component of proper $F$. It is a compact smooth complex manifold, and $T$ acts trivially on it. The Borel normal bundle is a complex vector bundle over $BT	imes F_0$; [F5] puts its base in the Thom theorem's scope. By [F6], $H_T^*(F_0;\mathbb Q)=H^*(BT;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}H^*(F_0;\mathbb Q)$. The weight subbundles from step 1.1 have ranks $m_\chi$ constant on $F_0$. Restricting the Borel normal bundle to $BT	imes\{x\}$, for any $x\in F_0$, gives $ igoplus_{\chi
e1}L_\chi^{\oplus m_\chi}$. By [F4] and the zero-section definition of Euler class, the restriction of $e_T(
u_F)$ is $w_0=\prod_{\chi
e1}u_\chi^{m_\chi}$. Each $u_\chi$ is a generator of $S_T$, so $w_0$ is invertible after localization.

Under the Künneth decomposition of step 2.2, write $e_T(\nu_F)=w_0+\eta$, where $\eta\in J_0\otimes_{\mathbb Q}H^*(BT;\mathbb Q)$; restriction to a point detects the degree-zero $F_0$ component $w_0$. By [F5], $J_0^N=0$ for some finite $N$, so $z=w_0^{-1}\eta$ has $z^N=0$ in the localized ring. Therefore $e_T(\nu_F)^{-1}=w_0^{-1}\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}(-z)^a$ is a finite inverse. The action fixes $([x:y],z)$ exactly when $z=0$, so $F=\mathbb P^1\times\{0\}\cong\mathbb P^1$ is smooth and proper. The morphism $X\to\mathrm{pt}$ is finite type and separated. After base change to $\mathbb A^1_s$, the equation $zs=1$ defines a closed subset of $X\times\mathbb A^1_s$, but its projection is $\mathbb A^1_s\setminus\{0\}$, which is not closed.
